links.reason: Verse 9 names பிறன்... பெண்டிரைக் காமுற்று as fools' love; verse 19 has பிறன்கடை நின்றொழுகு வான் among three who hang (தூங்குபவர்) by a thread. Both are the same book's list-verses on the same vice, but 19's door-loiterer is a physical-danger item beside elephant and snake, so 'judged by wanting and by result' is the shared theme, not a development.

23 has Civakan leave the city to bow to his mother (பயந்தாளைப் பணிந்த வாறும்) and 10 has her vow (நோற்ற வாறும்); both are consecutive patikam summary lines in story order. The claim that 'the patikam places the homecoming just before he turns to win back the kingdom' is not in 23's words.

845 shows Arkakirti mounted with his host; 962 shows him folding hands (கையிற் கூப்பினான்) to the Podanam king. This is story sequence; nothing in either verse sets pride beneath courtesy or qualifies one by the other.

53 says only Kama's arrows (காமவேள் கவர்கணை) were mingled in the land and no killing force troubled it; 66 says the king and women are bound by the flower-arrowed god's ordering (மலர்க் கணையினான்). The echo of Kama's arrows is real, but 66 is flagged uncertain and the link is closer to a repeated motif than a fulfilment.

605 tells hearers to tend ascetics (ஓம்பி) and also to strive at penance themselves (அருந்தவம் முயன்மின் யாரும்), which fits the chiding question of 263 (மறந்தார்கொல் மற்றை யவர்கள் தவம்). But the epic only states the rule the couplet implies; it does not answer or develop it, and the 'danger it guards against' in gains is not in the Tamil.

49 lists பத்தினி among the models and promises elsewhere explanation (வேறோர் இடத்து வெளிப்பட); 57 takes the பத்தினிப் பெண்டிர் comparison and ties conduct to ஒத்த பொருளான், so the later verse does gloss the earlier. The matching order of verses rests partly on the editor's sequence, but 57 names பத்தினி and 49 names பத்தினி directly.
links.text_issue: fragment; link leans on editor order of 51-60

links.reason: 2319's curse imagines becoming one who fears his wife (இல்லாளை யஞ்சி) and shames a guest; 904 says a man who fears his wife (மனையாளை அஞ்சும்) gains no glory in action. The words match in idea, but 904's mறுமை clause and its link to war are not in 2319, so the epic only illustrates and the other side gains nothing about weighing against cowardice.

1583 only has Civakan list the body's humours and tissues (குரைவளி பித்தோ டையே ... மூளை); it does not show him refusing or doing without grace. Siddhar 301 uses a similar body-catalogue but does not claim the catalogue is powerless; the supposed incompatibility is built from the poet's plea and the epic's unstated context.

Naladiyar 370 uses புதுப்புனல் to show friendship ending with income; Paripadal 7.84-86 prays that bathing in the Vaiyai may not be left (நின் படிந்து நீங்காமை). Neither claims the flood's permanence or impermanence against the other, and the Paripadal passage has a lacuna at 85; the 'tension' is two different uses of a river.

212 has Rudradattan saying even Indra follows the sharp-minded and that the king has one thought that will hurt the queen (ஓர் அறிவு). The verse shows a counsellor speaking, not a king refusing rebuke or the counsellor withdrawing, so the 'middle case' is imported; the connection to 448 (இடிப்பாரை) is thematic.

2011 has Civakan reach the guarded mansion disguised in old age (மூப்பெனு முகபடாம்); there is no Brahmin, no threats and no sparing in these lines. Kural 586's spy goes in the guise of renouncers (துறந்தார் படிவத்தர்) and examines; the note rests on 2014-2016 and stretches a lover's disguise into the spy's technique.

1396 has the friend recall her foretelling of trouble from a fanged snake (கட்டெயிற் றரவின் என்றேன்); 1271 narrates the snake biting Padumai (அரவு தீண்டி). The earlier prediction and its fulfilment are both in the Tamil. The reference to bringing Civakan is outside the verses but does not carry the claim.

1554 says those who trust moon-faced women's smiles (முறுவலம் பினார்) are reborn in sorrowful states; TM 204 warns against hearts burning for women who smile (முறுவல்செய் வார்மேல்). Both warn against the smile, but the epic does not use the etti image, so the 'epic gains the image' clause is false.

2124 has the freed one embrace the maiden முடிவு (முடிவென்னுங் கன்னி முலைமுயங்கி); 3117 has the king embrace கேவல மடந்தை. Both pictures of release as a bridal embrace are in the Tamil, and the difference (end vs omniscience) is correctly stated.
links.text_issue: 3117 flagged uncertain; 2125 has stray ங் but 2124 clean

links.reason: 1153 asks the root of the king's anger (முதலென் னென்பார்); 1156 has the people stop guessing (உரையொழி வாரும் ஆனார்). It is a crowd scene in sequence; 'dread grows' is not stated, and the verses between are not shown.

492 compares Govindai to the nectar the gods churned and says Padumukan lost all awareness but this one (ஓம்பா ஒழுக்கத்து உணர்வொன்றிலன்); it does not say he drinks. 216 says Saccandan drank nectar (அமிர்து உண்டு). The 'warning under the wedding' is imposed, and the note concedes the narrator blames no one.

52 mocks those who prattle of சத்தம் and சோதிடம் while neglecting death's urgency; 1281 gives a bird omen of life (ஆந்தை பாடும்) and a nimittikan speaking. The quatrain's scorn is for endless study instead of duty, not for fatalistic forecasting; the 'split divination' lesson is not in either Tamil text and the astrologer's failed verdict is not in 1281.

1824 says her enjoyment-lot ripened (போக பான்மையே பலித்தது) before the herald's words; 380 says fate (ஊழ்) is reached first even when one plans otherwise (சூழினுந் தான்முந் துறும்). The scene illustrates the couplet; it tests or limits it little, and the marker says no past-deed claim is made.

342 asks the cause of the king's love for the elephant (எனக்குதவக் காரணம் என்னெனக் கூறலும்); 346 answers that he was Gomukan (கோமுகன் ஒழிய ... நீ ஆயினை). A question and its answer within one dialogue. The 'cannot recall' detail is not in the Tamil, but the central structure holds.

339 says the drunk man became the elephant after death (ஆனைய தாயினன்); Siddhar 50 asks when the darkness of births as grass, beast, worm will leave (புல்லாய் விலங்காய் புழுவாய்). The verse supplies a cause that the Siddhar's line does not, but the pairing is broad rebirth-as-beast and the epic gains only a generic longing.

1721 shows the lord laying out jewels and cloth for guests to take (கவரக் காட்டினான்); 1737 has Tivittan give treasure to the messenger (நிதியின் நீத்தம் ... அருளினன்). Generosity is common to both, but a shared virtue is not a shared image, and 1737 says the messenger's joy, not Tivittan's, in the Tamil.

1132 has Gunamalai and her mother-in-law clinging to the ascetic's words (நோன்புணை) in grief; 2099 has Civakan say his survival came by her penance (நின் றவத்தின்). Nothing in 2099 links her grief-endurance to தவம்; the claim that her grief is 'renamed' penance is inferred, not stated.

2125 has 'உலக மலோக முடனே விழுங்கி' and 3082 has 'உலக மூன்றும் விழுங்கியிட் டலோக நுங்கி': a shared formula. But 3082 also names the cause (காதிப்போர் மன்னர் வீழ), i.e. the four ghati karmas, so 'only the Soolamani names the removal of coverings' is overstated.

619 shows Acuvakanthan so given to joy (களித்து) that he knows neither sun nor moon's temper; 539 bids one swollen with joy remember those ruined by negligence (இகழ்ச்சியின் கெட்டாரை). The verse shows no negligence or ruin, and does not show him ignoring the advice, so it is at most an illustration.

1004 shows the friend reading the bride's hint (குறிப்பு) and telling them to bow at the mother-in-law's feet; there is no smile in the Tamil. Kural 1274 is a lover's thought of a girl's smile-bud; the pairing joins unrelated acts of reading a signal.

783 has companions cut the chariot's ropes and bid the charioteer bring fresh horses (பூட்டு பாக ...); 773 calls help to a stricken foe valour's edge (ஊராண்மை மற்றதன் எஃகு). The chivalry fits, but cutting the ropes is also harm and the commentators' Rama example makes the 'new' lesson nearly the couplet's own.

784's noble begs from a base man's eyes (கீழ்மகன் கண்ணிரந்து) and earns blame; 1067 begs beggars not to beg of those who conceal (கரப்பார்). Base is not the same as miserly, so the note equates two different faults.
links.text_issue: 784 flagged uncertain; first two lines loose

links.reason: 951's five padas are water that wash karma (ஐம்பதங்கள் நீராக ... கழுவப்பட்டு) and give a god's birth; TM 2709 makes சிவாயநம a குளிகை that turns the body to gold. Both treat a mantra as agent of change with different outcomes, which is a real contrast but not a qualification of one by the other.

1122 says the merchant stood as if his life had gone (எஞ்சினான் போல நின்றான்) and was held up by the ascetic's words; Kural 269 says those who have the power of austerity can even leap past death (கூற்றம் குதித்தலும்). The merchant is not beyond death, and the words console; the couplet's word 'death' is stretched.

Naga Kumara Kaviyam 3 argues that smoke does not make people discard a bright lamp (புகைக்கொடி உள்ளுண்டென்றே ... விளக்கை இகழ்ச்சியின் நீப்பார் இல்லை); Naladiyar 151 says the noble pine at one stain unlike the moon. These speak about a poet's apology and about the sensitivity of noble persons, not the same thing.
838 only has the king order a host raised (சேனை பண்ணமைக்க) like a sea; 381 lists the six limbs. The note's 'escort' and 'display for allies' are not in 838, so the link is a shared word for army.

2079 has the ministers urge the king to give up the crown for the austerity (அணிமுடி துறமின்); Naladiyar 53 has the best renounce home and wealth on seeing impermanence. Both urge renunciation; the 'cost to others' is not in either text.

27 says Civakan, hearing dharma, renounced fearing kingship (அரசு அஞ்சித் துறந்த வாறும்); 2796 has the teacher say that taking the world is pain and guarding it greater (காவல் பெருந்துன்பம்). The teaching and the act it leads to are both in the Tamil.

1752 has the balls returning to the women like persistent lovers (காமுகர்போல்); Thiruppugazh 586 asks not to waste away over women whose palms ache from ball-play (பந்தாடி அங்கை நொந்தார்). The ball-play is shared, but neither makes a claim the other contradicts; a poem's description is not set against a devotee's plea.

901 has Maruci report to the king (தொழுது கூறலும்); 906 has the king speak to Maruci and send him to a mansion. 906 says nothing of preparations; this is sequence in a scene, not an answer or fulfilment.

1663 has the king bid a god become an elephant with spread face-cloth (படந்தவா முகத்தோர் வேழம்); Kural 1087 compares the breast cloth to a rutting elephant's face-cloth (கட்படாம்). The cloth is shared by word only; the epic verse does not say the elephant is for scaring women into his arms.

409 has the nimittikan foretell that within a month Tivittan will split a lion's mouth (சிங்கம் வாய் பிளந்திடும்); 707 has Tivittan vow to split its mouth (வாயைப் போழ்ந்து). The vow echoes the foretelling in near the same words, so the later verse takes up the earlier sign.

326 names Pazhaiyan of Por with his unerring spear (போஒர் கிழவோன் பழையன்); 44 has பழையன் பட்டென and Chenni's revenge, but does not say it is the lord of Por or the Cholas' champion. The pairing rests on the name alone, and 44 has no spear image.

1482 has the women's tears put out the king's wrath (அழுத கண்ணீர் ... முனிவென்னும் ஊழித் தீயும் அவிந்தது); 555 says tears of the afflicted are the weapon that wears down wealth (செல்வத்தைத் தேய்க்கும் படை). The contrast of quenching and wearing is partly right, but the note's 'victor ruled by weeping as the couplet says a king should dread' is not in the couplet.

396 says sin overtook the guileless ascetic and the hunger-fire made him give way in his vow (பாவம் வந்து அடைந்தது ... கொள்கையின் மெலிந்து); 261 defines penance as bearing the pain that comes (உற்றநோய் நோன்றல்). The epic shows a penitent failing the couplet's test and gives past sin as the reason, a limit the couplet does not state. The 'later resumed' detail is not in the verse.

1389 has the tree of suffering with ignorance as seed (பேதைமை வித்து) and desire as root (வேட்கை வேர்); 361 calls craving the seed of births (அவா ... வித்து). The order differs, but the note's claim that cutting desire would not uproot the tree is not in the verse and, for a tree, a cut root would end it.

270 reckons births past the sands (மணலும் ஆற்றா) and kin as two days' company; Siddhar 279 asks how many mothers and wives and births (எத்தனை எத்தனை). The shared reckoning is real; the claims about the king's composure 'with no god' and 'through scripture' rest on 271 and outside the verse.

1989 says household love brings many sufferings with its ties; 1990 says there is one thing won by vows, the effort for heavens and enjoyment lands. 1990 promises heaven, not relief of 1989's pain, so 'answer' is generous; this is two consecutive lines of one sermon.

996 has Gunamalai's heart burn like a sacrificial fire (வேள்வி முளரி); 1059 compares the mother's chastity to the flame of the Vedic sacrifice (மந்திரச் செந்தீ). The shared image is real, but 'discipline that marriage is meant to make of passion' is not in either verse.
